findings.title: Item-resume runs blocking git/cf/file I/O directly on the event loop
No load-test for the new run-lock concurrency path
findings.description: The Python rules require that "any code on the … concurrency … paths [requires] at least one load test" in the `tests/load/` tier, asserting latency/throughput/resource bounds, not just functional correctness. `run_lock.py` is new cross-process concurrency code, and the tests added for it live in `tests/pipeline/test_run_lock.py` / `tests/cli/commands/test_run_lock_cli.py`. Notably `test_a_killed_holder_releases_the_lock` does exercise real cross-process behavior (a child holds the flock, is killed, and the parent polls release with a 5s deadline), which partially covers the spirit — but there is no `tests/load/` entry for the lock (or the item-resume git paths), and nothing asserts the lock's timing/contention bounds under a realistic concurrent configuration. A small `tests/load/` test would close the tier requirement.

findings.title: Pruned runs leave their batch reports behind
findings.description: `prune` unlinks only the `{run_id}.json` state file, but slice 197 now writes a sibling `{run_id}.{step}.report.md` and `{run_id}.{step}.report.json` for every mutating/each run. `list_runs` correctly skips the `.report.json` files, so they don't corrupt listing — but they are never cleaned up, so orphaned reports accumulate in `~/.config/squadron/runs` (or the runs dir) as runs are pruned. Worth extending `prune` (or a companion sweep) to delete a run's report files when the run is pruned.

findings.title: Single-sourced flag/exit/param constants and fail-closed git semantics
findings.description: The flag kinds (`FlagKind`), exit codes (`ResumeExit`), reserved param keys (`control_params`), and report schema constants are each defined once and referenced everywhere (routing reads `flag_kind`, "never `reason`"; `reserved_param_error` drives both the `-p` rejection and the YAML `params:` block rejection). Git preconditioning fails closed (a non-slice branch or dirty target → REJECTED with "nothing changed"; an unknown state → HALTED), and rejections take the lock only briefly before touching nothing. This matches the "one value, one source" and fail-fast conventions well.
